subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users versus keep in logs or metadata?
rationale: The code already has token, model, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session keys/channel identifiers and exact token counts changes user-facing privacy and support behavior; automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Show redacted diagnostics
options.body: Expose model/provider, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

options.title: Keep specifics operator-only
options.body: Leave chat copy generic and document how operators can inspect logs or status metadata for detailed context-pressure facts.

options.title: Defer to broader context visibility
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for a broader context-visibility design to decide shared UI, logs, and channel-message behavior together.

recommendation.title: Show redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose model/provider, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.
